question.leadin: This emperor gave the "Jewel Voice Broadcast" to announce his country's surrender in World War II.
question.text: Name this emperor of an Asian country that fought against the US in the Pacific Theatre of World War II.
question.clue: The League of Blood supported greater autonomy for this man, whose most famous Prime Minister was executed after surviving self-inflicted gunshot wounds to the chest.

swap.leadin: This period succeeded the Tokugawa Shogunate.
swap.text: Name this period of rapid industrialization and modernization under a namesake emperor from 1869 to 1912 in Japan. The goals of the Emperor, restored to full power, were outlined in the Charter Oath.
swap.clue: Its goals were delineated in the Charter Oath, which expressed the desire break away from the "evil customs of the past."

question.leadin: Its founder was one of the three great unifiers of a certain country, along with Oda Nobunaga and Toyotomi Hideyoshi.
question.text: Name this shogunate, which was established after the Battle of Sekigahara and ruled from 1603 to 1868.
question.clue: One ruler of this period hosted the Convention of Kanagawa, and after a successful siege of Osaka Castle, its first ruler defeated the Toyotomi clan.

swap.text: Prior to the Perry Expedition, the only Japanese port that was largely open to foreigners was this city on the southern island of Kyushu. It later became the second city to be hit with an atomic bomb during World War II.
swap.clue: Trade between this city and Macau was carried out by non-American "black ships."

question.leadin: This battle saw the use of Portuguese arquebuses, and one side of this battle consisted of forces loyal to Toyotomi Hideyori.
question.text: Name this battle that saw the forces of Ishida Mitsunari and Mori Terumoto defeated by those of Tokugawa Ieyasu, thereby establishing his namesake shogunate.
question.clue: The capture of Konosu and Gifu Castles preceded this battle, whose decisive moment saw a staged round of arquebus fire signal a force of turncoats to attack the army of their initial ally Otani instead.

swap.text: The first military deployment of the atomic bomb occurred when the Enola Gay dropped the "Little Boy" over this city. A memorial dedicated to its victims was visited by Obama in May of 2016.
swap.clue: A bell with the phrase "know yourself" commemorates an incident in this city that created the first hibakusha ("HEE-ba-KOO-sha").

question.leadin: This treaty led to the Hibiya riot and the ceding of half of Sakhalin to Japan.
question.text: Name this treaty negotiated by Komura Jutaro and Sergei Witte, ending the Russo-Japanese War.
question.clue: For brokering this treaty, which the parties signed in Kittery, Maine, U.S. president Theodore Roosevelt received the Nobel Peace Prize.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Japanese history prior to the Meiji Restoration.
swap.text: This city was the capital of Japan until Emperor Meiji made Tokyo the capital in 1868.
swap.clue: Henry Stimson, the US Secretary of War, is said to have honeymooned here, and famously lobbied to have this city taken off the list of bombing targets during the Second World War despite significant protests from the military.

question.text: This first Shogunate began after Minamoto Yoritomo defeated the Tairas at the Battle of Dannoura in 1185. It was late dominated by the Hojo family.
question.clue: During much of this period, political control rested with the shikken or regent, an office which was held hereditarily by the Hojo Family.

swap.leadin: Of the hundreds of exploding balloons sent by this group to the U.S., only one managed to cause any damage, landing in Oregon and killing several schoolchildren who checked it out.
swap.text: Name this group within the Epidemic Prevention and Purification Department. A guy actually named Colonel Sanders brought it to the attention of Douglas MacArthur, who pardoned its leader in exchange for scientific data.
swap.answerHtml: Unit 731 [or Nana-san-ichi Butai, or Manchu Detachment 731, or 731 Regiment, or Ishii Unit]
swap.clue: This research group under the Kwantung Army committed some of the greatest Japanese crimes against humanity during the war. It was commanded by Shiro Ishii, who was pardoned by the United States after the war in exchange for his data.

question.leadin: Identify the following about a nation's history.
question.text: This period of Japanese history, which began after the move to from , lasted from 794-1185. It saw the rise of the bushi warrior as well as such great literature as Sei Shonagan's Pillow Book.
question.clue: Go-Sanjo and Shirawaka established the "cloistered emperor" or "insei" system during this period, which was dominated by the Fujiwara clan.

swap.text: After Japan's defeat in World War II, Hirohito managed to avoid the war crimes trials that condemned this Prime Minister. This man survived a 1945 suicide attempt before his execution by hanging in 1946.
swap.clue: This leader of the Chahar Expeditionary Force ordered troops to attack Hebei Province following the Marco Polo incident.

question.leadin: The "affliction of abiding in ignorance," meaning the absence of enlightenment, is compared to the act of "stopping" in this practice in the first section of the manual The Unfettered Mind.
question.text: Name this activity, whose central object is referred to as "life-giving" in a treatise on it translated by William Scott Wilson. This activity is the primary subject of Miyamoto Musashi's The Book of Five Rings.
question.answerHtml: swordfighting [or swordsmanship; or kenjutsu; prompt on martial arts; prompt on dueling]

swap.leadin: A leader of this domain obtained the first daguerreotype in Japan.
swap.text: Name this han that ruled much of southern Kyushu. This domain, which murdered a British merchant in the Namamugi incident, was dismantled after Saigo Takamori led it in rebellion.
swap.clue: The abolition of the han system led to the end of this region's control over the Ryukyu Islands.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about Russo-Japanese conflict FTPE.
question.text: This battle fought in 1939 was a response to an incursion of Mongolian cavalry into the territory of the Japanese puppet state of Manchukuo and resulted in a Russian victory that may have encouraged Japan to fight against the U.S. rather than Russia in the Pacific.
question.answerHtml: the Battle of Khalkin Gol (or the Battle of Khalkhin Lake or the Nomonhan Incident)
question.clue: This August 1939 clash on the Manchurian-Mongolian frontier resulted in a clear victory for Soviet armor commanded by the then-unknown General Zhukov over the Kwantung Army. Partly as a result, Stalin would be free to transfer Siberian forces to Europe following Operation Barbarossa.

swap.leadin: The massive temple complex of Todai-ji was constructed during this period as the center of a system of provincial temples known as kokubun-ji.
swap.text: Name this period of Japanese history in the 8th century that began with the establishment of Heijo-kyo as the capital. This period was followed by the Heian ("HAY-on") period.
swap.clue: This was the first time when emperors adopted the title of "tenno," and other innovations during this period, such as the institution of a Council of State, were adopted in order to imitate the government at Changan and important Tang Chinese institutions.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Jomon and Epi-Jomon cultures and peoples.
question.text: The term "Zoku" or "Epi-" Jomon refers to the persistence of Jomon patterns in northern Japan past when this culture superseded it further south. Wet rice agriculture became dominant in this culture's namesake period.

swap.text: The end of Hojo power came when this warlord overthrew Hojo Takatoki and established himself as shogun in 1336, thus beginning the Muromachi period, which was also known by his clan's name.

question.leadin: One of these structures is named after the Japanese word for chopsticks, Hashihaka, due to its resemblance to those utensils, and is thought to contain the body of the mythical queen Pimiko.
question.text: Name these keyhole-shaped megalithic tombs in Japan. The era lasting from roughly the 3rd century to the 6th century is named for them.
question.clue: A scholarly debate centers on whether two objects with raised left arms found in one of these places depict horse herders or dancers.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Empress Saimi, who reigned from 642 to 645 AD if we are to believe the historical record.
swap.text: That data appears in this chronicle, which like the Kojiki, is semi-mythical. The first petrochemical oil spill in ancient literature appears in this text's chronicle of Emperor Tenji.
swap.clue: This set of chronicles, the most comprehensive text available for scholarship on Ancient Japan. It was completed under the supervision of Prince Toneri and presented to Empress Gensho in the year 720.
